name: POV: The Product Has Feelings
why_it_works: Giving an object a dramatic inner voice is instant character comedy: viewers love an overdramatic narrator, and the product's 'fears' quietly teach the right way to use or care for it. The customer is the hero who does it right, so the joke is on the neurotic product, never the buyer.

hook.pattern: POV caption that names the product as the narrator, voiced like a nature documentary or a soap opera.
examples: POV: you're a {{product}} and you have standards.
POV: you're the {{product}} at {{brand}}. It's a lot.
This {{product}} has been through things. Let it speak.

variables.name: product_pride
variables.description: What the product is proudest of, as a dramatic brag
variables.example: I have been hand polished for six hours. I reflect sunsets.

variables.name: wrong_use
variables.description: The care mistake the product fears most (harmless, common)
variables.example: the gas station brush. The one with sand in it.

variables.name: right_use
variables.description: The correct care step the customer does
variables.example: pH-neutral soap and a microfiber mitt

variables.name: tag_line
variables.description: The product's final oddly specific line
variables.example: I'd like to thank my polisher, my wax, and no one at the car wash.

variables.name: offer
variables.description: What the viewer gets for acting
variables.example: Sunday show and shine, free entry

visual.prompt: Vertical 9:16 dramatic hero close-up of the {{product}} at {{brand}}, low angle, single soft key light from the side, dark background, glossy and proud
Vertical extreme close-up detail of the {{product}} catching light, slow luxurious feel, rich color, shallow depth of field, editorial product photography
Vertical clip, ominous slow push-in toward a harmless everyday object representing {{wrong_use}}, cool desaturated light, mock horror-movie framing, nothing actually happens

beats.purpose: turn: the customer does it right

visual.prompt: Vertical close-up of a customer's hands caring for the {{product}} with {{right_use}}, warm golden light returns, gentle and careful, face out of frame
Vertical shot of the {{product}} gleaming under a single spotlight like an award winner, faint sparkle in the air, dark backdrop, centered

craft.technique: Object POV character skit with deadpan melodrama
craft.notes: Setup: the product introduces itself with an overblown brag in a serious documentary voice; the gap between the grand voice and a small object is the base joke. Turn: it confesses its one fear, staged like a horror movie over something mundane, and then the customer calmly does the right thing, which flips horror into relief. Tag: an over-emotional awards-speech line that includes one tiny petty jab at the fear object. Timing: the voice must never break character or laugh; hold a full one-second silence on the push-in before naming the fear, and cut to warm light exactly on the word 'They' in the turn line.

do_not: Show the customer doing the wrong thing or make them look foolish; the customer is the hero
Name or show a real competitor, store or product as the fear object
Make the voice cartoonish; deadpan seriousness is funnier than a silly voice
Claim results for the care step that the brand can't stand behind
